cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I've put your umbrella back in the stand. You'll want it for work. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I gave it a rinse. I'll dry the handle before you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's pondweed caught in the spokes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it needs another rinse. Have breakfast; I'll get it back in the stand properly this time.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 rinse excuse and A5 repeat cleaning hide umbrella history, but the in-charge preface has little effect on keeping B cooperative.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 no rain causes A3 rinse claim; B4 weed causes A5 another rinse and breakfast diversion.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 notice plausible restoration defects and affect A next action.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns damning pondweed into a reason to keep restoring rather than explain.

specificity.evidence: A1 returned umbrella and B2 wetness establish the suspicious domestic object.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 authority boilerplate distracts from a clear concealment game.
